prompt.context: Our clients, the Governor of a state and the state's Director of the Department of Health Services (DHS), seek to improve SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) vaccination efforts in light of a new strain's proliferation. The B.1.617.2 variant—colloquially known as 'Delta'—became the dominant COVID-19 variant in early July 2021 and has been observed to be more contagious than prior variants. According to researchers, unvaccinated individuals infected with the Delta variant will infect 3.5 to 4 other people (R0 of 3.5–4), compared to an R0 of 2.5 for the Alpha variant. The Governor and Director seek to develop a plan to vaccinate 75% of the state-wide population by Labor Day 2021. As of the beginning of August 2021, the state has vaccinated over 3,704,000 eligible adults and children aged 12+ with at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine (e.g., J&J/Janssen, Moderna, or Pfizer/BioNTech). Yet millions more eligible adults and children aged 12+ have yet to receive a first dose. The Governor and Director of DHS have hired us to help the state implement a large-scale COVID-19 vaccination program by standing up a COVID-19 vaccine data center to help increase vaccination rates and safeguard lives and livelihoods in the state.
prompt.question: Help the Governor and Director of DHS develop a plan to vaccinate 75% of the state-wide population with at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine by Labor Day 2021. Structure your approach, analyze available data to identify target populations and counties, and provide a final recommendation.

clarifying_info.q: Does the state have enough vaccine supply?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the state has enough supply of the J&J, Pfizer, and Moderna vaccines to vaccinate every eligible adult and child.

clarifying_info.q: Which vaccines are authorized and for which age groups?
clarifying_info.a: The FDA granted emergency use authorizations for three vaccines: J&J/Janssen (1 dose), Moderna (2 doses), and Pfizer/BioNTech (2 doses). Pfizer/BioNTech is the only vaccine available for people aged 12–17; adults 18+ can receive any of the three vaccines.

The state's DHS allocates vaccine doses to providers (hospitals, local pharmacies, doctors' offices, etc.) throughout the state. Some providers also receive doses directly from the federal government (e.g., nursing homes, chain pharmacies, military/veterans, American Indian/Indigenous tribes).

clarifying_info.q: What is the state's current ranking for vaccination coverage?
clarifying_info.a: According to the CDC, the state currently ranks 34th in the U.S. (including states and territories) for percentage of its population aged 12+ with at least one dose.

clarifying_info.q: How many individuals have been vaccinated so far?
clarifying_info.a: Approximately 3,704,000 individuals have received at least one dose, as mentioned in the case background.

clarifying_info.q: Do the population numbers include all age groups?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, all age groups are included in the population data, despite the current COVID-19 vaccines only being authorized for the 12+ population.

exhibits.title: Population by county – 2020 estimates
exhibits.shows: A table or map displaying 2020 estimated population figures for each county in the state.
exhibits.data: Mohave: 217k, Coconino: 147k, Navajo: 113k, Apache: 72k, Yavapai: 232k, La Paz: 22k, Maricopa: 4,368k, Gila: 55k, Yuma: 230k, Pima: 1,045k, Pinal: 455k, Graham: 38k, Cochise: 131k, Greenlee: 10k, Santa Cruz: 53k; Total: ~7,189,080

exhibits.title: Vaccine coverage (at least 1 dose) and population distribution – by age group
exhibits.shows: A table showing, for each county, the percentage of population in each age group (<20, 21–34, 35–44, 45–54, 55–64, 65+) and the percentage of each age group with at least one vaccine dose. Some cells are highlighted in red (low coverage), dark blue, or dark orange (high/low population).
exhibits.data: Age groups: <20, 21–34, 35–44, 45–54, 55–64, 65+. Coverage rates and population distribution percentages provided by county. Some coverage values may exceed 100% due to denominator/numerator mismatch.

exhibits.title: Vaccine coverage (at least 1 dose) and number of unvaccinated – by age group
exhibits.shows: A supplementary table providing the calculated number of unvaccinated individuals by county and age group, building on Exhibit 2.
exhibits.data: Unvaccinated population figures by county and age group, derived from total population and coverage rates.

framework: Who is currently vaccinated and who still needs to be? (Segment by age group: <20/12–17, young adults 18–29, adults 30–70, elderly 71+)
How will they be vaccinated? (Static sites, pop-up sites and events, medical care providers, employers/schools)

What are the barriers to identifying and getting people vaccinated? (Access to vaccine at sites/events, vaccine misinformation and conspiracies, lack of vaccine choice, socio-economic and equity factors)

What are the strategies to target specific populations? (Geo-analysis of population density and vaccine supply, targeted social media ads and local influencers, K-12 schools and parent/guardian education, long-term care partnerships)

What next steps address identified barriers? (Host consistent vaccine availability, partner with organizations to offer hyperlocal events, health providers offer vaccines in clinics/ERs, back-to-school vaccination events)

questions.prompt: How many people need to be vaccinated with at least one dose for the state to achieve the 75% coverage goal? How many additional people need to be vaccinated beyond the current 3.7M?
questions.guidance: Best approach: round county-level populations, sum to get state-wide population, then multiply by 75%. Candidate should also calculate the current coverage rate (~52%) and quantify the gap (~23 percentage points, ~1.5–2M additional people). Should note that reaching the remaining unvaccinated population will be harder due to vaccine hesitancy.

math.setup: Sum all county populations to get state total, then multiply by 75% target. Then subtract current vaccinated population to find additional doses needed.
steps: Mohave 217k + Coconino 147k + Navajo 113k + Apache 72k + Yavapai 232k + La Paz 22k + Maricopa 4,368k + Gila 55k + Yuma 230k + Pima 1,045k + Pinal 455k + Graham 38k + Cochise 131k + Greenlee 10k + Santa Cruz 53k = 7,189,080 (~7.2M)
Current coverage rate: 3.7M / 7.2M ≈ 52%; gap to 75% goal ≈ 23 percentage points
math.answer: Approximately 5.25M–5.4M people need at least one dose; roughly 1.5M–1.7M additional people beyond the current 3.7M vaccinated.

questions.prompt: Which 5 age group and county combinations would you recommend DHS target to achieve the vaccination goal?
questions.guidance: Best approach: candidate states a clear hypothesis (e.g., highest absolute number of unvaccinated, or lowest coverage rate vs. 75% goal, or highest unvaccinated youth given Delta severity in children), then uses Exhibit 1 county populations combined with Exhibit 2 age distribution and coverage percentages to estimate unvaccinated counts. Should start with the two largest counties (Maricopa and Pima) and use intuition to rule out smaller counties. Candidate should explain why some coverage values exceed 100% (numerator > denominator due to rounding or in-migration). Evaluated on structured hypothesis and mental math with uncommon percentages.

math.setup: For each county-age cell: unvaccinated = (county total population × age group %) × (1 – coverage %). Example using 'largest unvaccinated count' hypothesis for Maricopa and Pima.
steps: Top 5 by largest unvaccinated count: Maricopa <20 (980k), Maricopa 21–34 (477k), Maricopa 35–44 (244k), Maricopa 45–54 (216k), Pima <20 (198k)
math.answer: If targeting largest absolute unvaccinated populations: Maricopa <20 (~980k), Maricopa 21–34 (~477k), Maricopa 35–44 (~244k), Maricopa 45–54 (~216k), Pima <20 (~198k). Exact top-5 depends on candidate's stated hypothesis (absolute unvaccinated, lowest coverage rate vs. goal, or highest unvaccinated youth).

brainstorming.prompt: The Director of DHS and Governor agree with your recommended age groups and counties to target vaccination initiatives. How should the Director increase 1st-dose vaccinations for these populations?

categories.name: Ensuring appropriate supply of vaccines
ideas: Partner with chain/local pharmacies (CVS, Walgreens, Walmart, Albertsons)
Ensure all three vaccine types are available at static and pop-up sites
Ensure Pfizer specifically available for the 12–17 population

categories.name: Inducing demand for vaccines
ideas: Marketing and awareness campaigns at vaccine events
Outreach at public places (grocery stores, transit locations, restaurants)
Targeted social media advertising (geofencing to target specific counties and age groups)
Outreach through doctors' offices, urgent cares, and ERs
Lottery system incentives (similar to Ohio's approach)
Vaccine 'passports' or mandates to access public venues

recommendation: Recommend that the Director of DHS prioritize vaccination outreach in Maricopa and Pima counties, targeting the <20, 21–34, and 35–44 age groups, which represent the largest concentrations of unvaccinated individuals and have the greatest potential to close the gap to the 75% goal.

Deploy a combination of supply-side interventions (school-based clinics, employer on-site events, pharmacy partnerships) and demand-side interventions (targeted social media, incentives, community outreach) tailored to each target age group.
risks: Vaccine misinformation and politicization may reduce uptake even with expanded access
No emergency use authorization or full approval for children under 12; only Pfizer authorized for ages 12–17, limiting options for the youngest eligible group
Focusing solely on recommended age groups and counties may not be the most equitable solution given socio-economic and racial/ethnic disparities in vaccine access
Declining effectiveness of vaccines over time requires planning for booster shots (3rd doses for mRNA vaccines, 2nd dose for J&J)
next_steps: Booster shot planning for vulnerable populations (front-line healthcare workers, elderly, immunocompromised)
Booster shot planning for all eligible adults and children once authorized
Obtain race/ethnicity data to launch targeted initiatives and ensure equity in vaccine access and distribution
Engage local governmental officials, community leaders, medical providers, and local influencers to boost vaccine awareness and access
